agency: Nebraska Department of Roads (NDOR, now NDOT)
document: Design Aids of NU I-Girder Bridges (NDOR / University of Nebraska-Lincoln), section 1.1 Girder Section Properties, Figure 1 and Table 1

source.direct_access: dot.nebraska.gov refuses TCP connections from this machine (ECONNREFUSED); Wayback snapshot 2025-05-15 used
source.date: PDF created 2010-08-01; cites AASHTO LRFD 2007 and NDOR BOPP 2009

units: figure inches (rounded conversions of a metric design); implemented in the metric nominal values listed in Table 1 and the standard metric NU template
geometry_notes: Table 1 gives heights, web and flange widths in mm (900-2000, 150, 1225, 975); Figure 1 gives the flange stack in rounded inches, each the conversion of a round metric value (2.56=65, 1.75~45, 5.3~135, 5.5~140, 7.9~200, 2~50 mm). The metric values are used.
Taper extension lines end on the web faces; R200 web fillets and R50 flange-corner radii are tangent arcs (64 segments).

Estimate: a 20 mm x 20 mm soffit chamfer, not shown on Figure 1, is included. Without it every size is +527 mm2 (+0.08%) in area and +0.09% in I against Table 1; with it residuals fall to <=0.01% area and <=0.05% I. Soffit chamfers of this size appear on the MoDOT NU (3/4 in) and MTO NU (20 mm) drawings, but the value here is justified only by the area fit.
Table 1 NU1350 metric inertia (126,841 x10^6 mm4) disagrees with its inch value (302,334 in4 = 125,840 x10^6 mm4); the inch value is used and the metric cell pinned as a source typo.
Not asserted identical to the current (2026) NDOT BDM Figure 5.4 or to other states' NU drawings.
